title: The Spatial Working Memory Precision - a Biomarker for Optimizing the Methylphenidate Dosage in adult ADHD
summary:
Cognitive impairments, particularly in working memory, are a core feature of many psychiatric disorders – including ADHD. Working memory allows us to temporarily store and process information, which is essential for language, learning, and problem-solving. When this ability is impaired, it can significantly impact daily functioning.
Approximately 5% of the population is affected by ADHD. In about one-third of cases, symptoms persist into adulthood. In addition to attention and behavioral difficulties, many individuals with ADHD also show marked cognitive deficits. One potentially important, but underexplored, aspect is working memory precision – the accuracy with which information is retained in memory.
From a neurobiological perspective, ADHD is associated with altered dopamine signaling in the brain. Medications such as methylphenidate (MPH), commonly used to treat ADHD, act on this dopamine system. However, individual responses to these medications vary widely. Part of this variability may be linked to differences in working memory function and underlying dopaminergic activity.
Studies suggest that moderate doses of MPH can enhance working memory performance, while higher doses may lead to deterioration – pointing to a dose-dependent, nonlinear relationship.
This study aims to investigate whether working memory precision can serve as a biomarker to predict the optimal individual dosage of MPH. This could help avoid cognitive side effects and improve treatment outcomes. In addition, polygenic risk scores may offer further insight into individual treatment responses based on genetic factors.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Normal or corrected vision
-Signed declaration of consent
-For patients: Completed diagnosis of ADHD (according to DSM-5) (checked according to the German version of the DIVA 2.0 interview)
-For patients: Global Impressions Scale (CGI) ≥ 4 & ADHD Rating Scale for Adults (ADHD-RS-V) ≥ 30
Exclusion criteria:
-Persons with a current or past neurological disease
-Persons with a serious somatic illness (incl. cancer, chemotherapy, etc.)
-Drug use (incl. marijuana) in the last 28 days
-Premorbid IQ < 70
-Color blindness (verified by Ishihara test)
-For control subjects: current or past psychiatric illness or first-degree relatives with a current or past psychiatric illness
-In patients: Contraindication to methylphenidate (MPH)
-In patients: Use of methylphenidate or other stimulants in the past 6 months
-In patients: current comorbid severe psychiatric illness (including active alcohol and drug abuse)
